reviews.label: First Light (`EchoLaunch`)
reviews.purpose: Coordinates the one reliable beginning of the application, ordered startup, launch status, diagnostics, and final handoff.
reviews.example: A Rescuers2D build opens through one Boot scene, validates configuration, shows the startup sequence, then hands off to the Main Menu.
reviews.completionNote: Core teach-back passed; final synthesis assisted.

reviews.label: The Observatory (`EchoDiagnostics`)
reviews.purpose: Collects and presents validation, runtime health, performance, and package diagnostics without owning the systems being observed.
reviews.example: A development overlay reveals a duplicate persistent root, the active scene, frame time, and why First Light failed a startup step.
reviews.pauseNote: Introductory layer began, then paused by ADR-004. Resume immediately before EchoDiagnostics implementation. Not complete.

reviews.label: The Accord (`EchoSettings`)
reviews.purpose: Owns global preferences, defaults, edit/apply/cancel transactions, validation, persistence, migration, and safe display rollback.
reviews.example: A player changes master volume, resolution, subtitles, and reduced motion; Cancel restores the previous effective settings safely.

reviews.label: The Passage (`EchoSceneFlow`)
reviews.purpose: Owns normal runtime scene-transition requests, loading phases, progress, locking, recovery, and destination validation.
reviews.example: The player leaves the Main Menu, sees a fade and loading status, enters Level 1, and cannot trigger a second conflicting load.

reviews.label: The Pulse (`EchoGameState`)
reviews.purpose: Owns high-level runtime state, temporary override scopes, nested pause reasons, time policy, and cursor coordination intent.
reviews.example: Opening a pause menu adds a pause scope; a confirmation modal adds another; closing them out of order does not unpause gameplay early.

reviews.label: Resonance (`Jukebot`)
reviews.purpose: Owns music, SFX, ambience, pooled voices, playback handles, concurrency, crossfades, and mixer routing.
reviews.example: Exploration music crossfades into danger music while a shield bash and ambience continue independently without duplicated tracks.

reviews.label: The Will (`EchoInput`)
reviews.purpose: Owns input contexts, reason-based locks, device detection, rebinding transactions, override data, and glyph resolution.
reviews.example: Opening inventory disables gameplay actions, enables UI navigation, and changes prompts from keyboard keys to controller glyphs.

reviews.label: The Looking Glass (`EchoUI`)
reviews.purpose: Owns reusable surface registration, scoped navigation, independent windows/HUD/overlays, focus/visibility presentation, Motifs, primitives, and UI authoring tooling without becoming game-state/input/domain authority.
reviews.example: A Main Menu navigates to Settings and Back while an independent Inventory-style window can coexist; later a registry-driven Menu for Menus can toggle authored surfaces by stable ID.

reviews.label: The Chronicle (`EchoSave`)
reviews.purpose: Owns save slots, immutable generations, manifests, participant payloads, migration, integrity, backup, and corruption recovery.
reviews.example: An autosave is interrupted; the next launch rejects the incomplete generation and restores the most recent verified save.
reviews.completionNote: Teach-back completed across persistence/runtime/lifetime separation, participants, transactional safety, load recovery, lifecycle, operation gating, dirty state, and provider seams. ESV-M1-01 explicitly activated.

reviews.label: The Workshop (`EchoGameStarter`)
reviews.purpose: Owns Editor-time package selection, dry-run planning, installation coordination, project generation, repair, receipts, and removal guidance.
reviews.example: A new game-jam project selects Launch, UI, Input, Audio, and no game saves, previews every file, then generates a visible starter foundation.

reviews.label: Impact (`EchoFeedback`)
reviews.purpose: Coordinates semantic feedback recipes across camera, timing, haptics, flashes, UI, and audio providers without owning those providers.
reviews.example: A C4 explosion requests one recipe that triggers camera shake, hit stop, rumble, flash, UI punch, and a Jukebot cue.

reviews.label: The Wellspring (`EchoPool`)
reviews.purpose: Owns reusable object pools, prewarming, generational leases, return safety, capacity, exhaustion policy, scopes, and diagnostics.
reviews.example: Bullets, rescue markers, and temporary VFX are reused instead of repeatedly instantiated and destroyed during a busy level.

reviews.label: The Ascent (`EchoProgression`)
reviews.purpose: Owns unlocks, access rules, checkpoints, progression-node completion, local rank snapshots, password grants, and progression state.
reviews.example: Rescuers2D validates a level password, unlocks Level 4, records the checkpoint, and exposes access state to the level-select screen.

reviews.label: The Foundry (`EchoBuildTools`)
reviews.purpose: Owns repeatable build recipes, preflight validation, version stamping, safe output handling, receipts, manifests, and release preparation.
reviews.example: A WebGL itch.io build validates scenes and licenses, stamps the version, cleans only its owned folder, builds, and writes checksums.

reviews.label: Many Tongues (`EchoLocalization`)
reviews.purpose: Owns locale authority, localized-reference resolution, fallback, regional formatting, font/script policy, pseudolocalization, and diagnostics.
reviews.example: Changing to Spanish refreshes UI and dialogue references, applies regional number formats, and reports a missing glyph before release.

reviews.label: Voices (`EchoDialogue`)
reviews.purpose: Owns speaker and conversation definitions, deterministic node traversal, lines, choices, conditions, commands, history, and session snapshots.
reviews.example: A Hackulos spell vendor greets the player, checks a quest condition, offers two choices, and dispatches a typed command to grant spells.

reviews.label: The Path (`EchoObjectives`)
reviews.purpose: Owns objectives, runs, graph progress, counters, flags, timers, repeatability, tracking, completion, and idempotent reward delivery ledgers.
reviews.example: The rat-tail quest tracks a kill, item collection, return, exact combine, and bag placement without storing inventory or dialogue truth.

reviews.label: The Vault (`EchoInventory`)
reviews.purpose: Owns item/container definitions, fungible stacks, unique item instances, capacity, filters, queries, atomic transfers, and generic equipment storage.
reviews.example: A bag holds stacked rat tails and one uniquely damaged sword; moving or equipping them succeeds completely or makes no change.

reviews.label: The Hand (`EchoInteraction`)
reviews.purpose: Owns interaction offers, detection, availability, focus, prompts, session lifetimes, holds, cancellation, and execution routing.
reviews.example: The same ladder offers Pick Up or Climb depending on context; the package selects the offer while project code performs the outcome.

reviews.label: The Eye (`EchoCamera`)
reviews.purpose: Owns camera channels, target registration, modes, priorities, blends, bounds, zones, impulses, and backend negotiation.
reviews.example: Switching from Firefighter to Specialist changes the camera target while a rescue zone adds bounds and Impact requests a shake.

reviews.label: The Fellowship (`EchoCharacters`)
reviews.purpose: Owns character definitions, durable roster members, selection contexts, groups, spawning, runtime actors, respawn, and exclusive control ownership.
reviews.example: Rescuers2D switches Firefighter, Riot Officer, and Specialist while preserving one roster and handing control to the selected actor.

reviews.label: The Vessel (`EchoControllers`)
reviews.purpose: Owns actor-bound controller hosts, normalized intent, local motors, locomotion state, focused capabilities, physics policy, and semantic movement events.
reviews.example: A side-view specialist walks and jumps using the platformer preset while Hackulos uses an independent top-down 2D preset.

reviews.label: The Crucible (`EchoCrafting`)
reviews.purpose: Owns recipe definitions, exact combines, standard matching, previews, requirements, idempotency, and one-provider atomic crafting transactions.
reviews.example: Hackulos combines a rat tail and human eye inside a quest bag without importing a full profession or production-queue system.

reviews.label: The Convergence (`EchoMultiplayer`)
reviews.purpose: Defines provider-neutral sessions, participants, readiness, roles, authority, travel, spawn/ownership, security, adapters, and prototype gates.
reviews.example: A future co-op prototype hosts a lobby, synchronizes a scene change, assigns characters, validates an interaction, and handles disconnects.

reviews.label: Instinct (`EchoAI`)
reviews.purpose: Defines reusable stimuli, perception memory, target scoring, typed context, scheduling, behavior seams, navigation contracts, and AI diagnostics.
reviews.example: A passive rat notices nearby food while an aggressive humanoid scores threats, chases, and later flees at low health using project-authored rules.

reviews.label: Clash (`EchoCombat`)
reviews.purpose: Defines provider-neutral combat requests, targetability, relations, deterministic modifiers, target-owned transactions, outcomes, and defeat events.
reviews.example: A shield bash submits damage and stagger requests; the target’s health/posture authority commits the actual resource changes.

reviews.label: Arcana (`EchoAbilities`)
reviews.purpose: Defines ability grants, loadouts, activation, costs, charges, cooldowns, casting, interruption, targeting, effects, persistence, and authority seams.
reviews.example: A Necromancer begins Life Drain, commits mana at the chosen point, channels repeated effects, and can be interrupted under authored rules.

reviews.label: The Atlas (`EchoWorld`)
reviews.purpose: Defines durable worlds, zones, locations, travel graphs, scene bindings, entry/spawn markers, discovery, fast travel, map snapshots, and world-state routing.
reviews.example: Devroth contains semantic towns and wilderness locations that survive scene renames and route travel through The Passage.
